prompt.adult: Proverbs 6:6 tells the sluggard to consider the ways of a certain creature and be wise. Which creature?
prompt.child: Proverbs 6:6 tells a lazy person to go and learn from a small creature. Which one?
prompt.teen: Proverbs 6:6 sends the sluggard to study one of God's creatures. Which one?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 6:6, to what creature is the sluggard told to go and consider her ways?

verses.text: Go to the ant, you sluggard! Consider her ways and be wise,

explanation.adult: The creature is named in the first words of Proverbs 6:6, right after "Go to."
explanation.child: Look at the very start of Proverbs 6:6. The creature comes right after "Go to."
explanation.teen: 6:6 opens with a command and names the creature at once. Read the first phrase.
explanation.older: The creature is named in the opening imperative of 6:6.

teaching.extended_explanation: Proverbs 6:6 speaks directly to the sluggard, someone who avoids work, and tells him to watch a small creature and learn from her. Read the first words of the verse.
teaching.takeaway: Proverbs 6:6 says, "Go to the ant, you sluggard! Consider her ways and be wise."

prompt.adult: Proverbs 22:7 describes what happens between someone who borrows and someone who lends. What does the borrower become to the lender?
prompt.child: Proverbs 22:7 talks about borrowing. What does it say a borrower becomes to the person who lent to him?
prompt.teen: Proverbs 22:7 makes a point about debt. What is the borrower to the lender?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 22:7, what is the borrower to the lender?

verses.text: The rich rules over the poor, And the borrower is servant to the lender.

explanation.adult: Read the second line of Proverbs 22:7, right after "the borrower is."
explanation.child: Look at the end of Proverbs 22:7. The word comes right after "the borrower is."
explanation.teen: 22:7 has two lines that make the same kind of point. Read the second line closely.
explanation.older: The second clause of 22:7 names the borrower's position relative to the lender.

teaching.extended_explanation: Proverbs 22:7 is a short saying about power and money. Its first line speaks of the rich and the poor, and its second line describes what borrowing does to a person. Read the words right after "the borrower is."
teaching.takeaway: The borrower is servant to the lender.

prompt.adult: Proverbs 6:8 says a small creature stores up supplies and food. What does 6:7 say it does all this without?
prompt.child: This tiny creature stores up food all on its own. What does Proverbs 6:7 say it does not have?
prompt.teen: 6:7-8 describes a creature that prepares ahead with no one making it. What does 6:7 say it lacks?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 6:7, what does the creature lack, even though it provides its supplies?

choices.text: No nest, burrow or place to rest

verses.text: Which, having no captain, Overseer or ruler,
Provides her supplies in the summer, And gathers her food in the harvest.

explanation.adult: Proverbs 6:7 is one short line. Read it right after "having."
explanation.child: Read Proverbs 6:7. It lists three things the creature does not have.
explanation.teen: 6:7 lists three things the creature does not have, and 6:8 shows the work still gets done. Read 6:7 closely.
explanation.older: 6:7 names three things the creature does without; 6:8 then describes its work.

teaching.extended_explanation: Proverbs 6:6-8 points to a small creature as a teacher. Verse 7 says what it does not have, and verse 8 shows that it still prepares its food. Read 6:7 for what it is missing.
teaching.takeaway: She has no captain, overseer or ruler, yet she provides her supplies.

prompt.child: Proverbs 10:4 compares two kinds of hands. Whose hand brings riches?
prompt.teen: 10:4 sets one kind of hand against another. Which hand does it say makes rich?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 10:4, whose hand makes rich?

verses.text: He who has a slack hand becomes poor, But the hand of the diligent makes rich.

explanation.adult: Read the second line of Proverbs 10:4, right after "But the hand of."
explanation.child: Look at the end of Proverbs 10:4, after "But the hand of."
explanation.teen: 10:4 contrasts two hands with "But." Read who the second hand belongs to.
explanation.older: The second clause of 10:4 names the owner of the hand that makes rich.

prompt.adult: Proverbs 11:24 describes one person who scatters freely and another who holds back what he should give. What happens to the one who scatters?
prompt.child: Proverbs 11:24 talks about a person who gives freely and one who holds back what he should give. What happens to the giver?
prompt.teen: 11:24 sounds surprising: one person scatters, another withholds. What does it say happens to the one who scatters?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 11:24, what is the outcome for the one who scatters?

verses.text: There is one who scatters, yet increases more; And there is one who withholds more than is right, But it leads to poverty.
The generous soul will be made rich, And he who waters will also be watered himself.

explanation.adult: Read the first line of Proverbs 11:24, right after "scatters, yet."
explanation.child: Look at the start of Proverbs 11:24. The result comes right after "scatters, yet."
explanation.teen: 11:24 has a surprise in the first line. Read what follows "yet."
explanation.older: The first clause of 11:24 states the unexpected outcome after "yet."

teaching.extended_explanation: Proverbs 11:24-25 talks about generosity. The first line of 11:24 describes someone who scatters, giving freely, and uses the word "yet" because the result is not what you might expect. Read the words after "yet."
teaching.takeaway: The one who scatters increases more.

prompt.adult: Proverbs 6:10-11 warns against "a little sleep, a little slumber," and 10:5 contrasts two sons at harvest time. According to 10:5, who is the wise son?
prompt.child: Proverbs 6:10-11 warns about sleeping when there is work to do. Proverbs 10:5 compares two sons. Which son does it call wise?
prompt.teen: 6:10-11 warns about "a little folding of the hands," and 10:5 picks up the same idea. Who is called a wise son in 10:5?
prompt.older: Connecting Proverbs 6:10-11 with 10:5, whom does 10:5 call a wise son?

choices.text: He who sells at the market
He who rests until the rains

verses.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep—
So shall your poverty come on you like a prowler, And your need like an armed man.
He who gathers in summer is a wise son; He who sleeps in harvest is a son who causes shame.

explanation.adult: Read the first line of Proverbs 10:5. The wise son is described before the words "is a wise son."
explanation.child: Look at the start of Proverbs 10:5. It tells what the wise son does.
explanation.teen: 6:10-11 shows what too much rest leads to; 10:5 shows the opposite. Read the first line of 10:5.
explanation.older: The first clause of 10:5 describes the wise son's action and timing; the second describes the other son.

teaching.extended_explanation: Proverbs 6:10-11 warns that putting off work, a little at a time, can leave a person in need. Proverbs 10:5 makes a similar point with two sons: one son is called wise and the other causes shame. Read the first line of 10:5.
teaching.takeaway: He who gathers in summer is a wise son.

prompt.adult: Proverbs 13:11 says wealth gained by dishonesty will be diminished, and 11:28 warns against trusting in one's wealth. What does 11:28 say the righteous will flourish like?
prompt.child: Proverbs warns that dishonest money shrinks and that trusting in money leads to a fall. What does 11:28 say the righteous will grow like?

prompt.older: Reading Proverbs 11:28 alongside 13:11, to what are the righteous compared as they flourish?

verses.text: He who trusts in his riches will fall, But the righteous will flourish like foliage.
Wealth gained by dishonesty will be diminished, But he who gathers by labor will increase.

explanation.adult: Read the end of Proverbs 11:28, right after "the righteous will flourish."
explanation.child: Look at the last words of Proverbs 11:28, after "will flourish."
explanation.teen: 11:28 sets falling against flourishing. Read the picture at the end of the verse.
explanation.older: The simile closing 11:28 describes how the righteous flourish; read it closely.

teaching.extended_explanation: Proverbs 13:11 contrasts wealth gained dishonestly with wealth gathered by honest labor. Proverbs 11:28 contrasts a person who trusts in his money with the righteous, and it ends with a picture. Read the last words of 11:28.
teaching.takeaway: The righteous will flourish like foliage.
